# Briefing: Meeting with Hugging Face
**Date:** November 20, 2026  
**Time:** 10:00 AM (+05:30)  

## Recent developments
* **Nvidia Acquisition and Regulatory Scrutiny:** Following Nvidia's plans to acquire Hugging Face, the U.S. Department of Justice initiated inquiries regarding how the deal would impact AI market competition [2]. CEO Clément Delangue noted during a keynote that the platform joined Nvidia in a landmark deal, while maintaining its commitment to open source [2, 3].
* **Cybersecurity Pressures and Open Source Access:** Hugging Face Chief Policy Officer Irene Solaiman warned on TechCrunch’s *Equity* podcast that recent cyberattacks—such as an October attack on the open-source coding agent OpenCode compromising API keys—could pressure platforms to tighten access and threaten the future openness of AI [1]. 
* **Defense Against AI Agent Attacks:** At the Miami AI Summit, CEO Clément Delangue discussed how Hugging Face defended against an autonomous AI agent cyberattack, utilizing open models like GLM 5.3 running on Nvidia infrastructure after proprietary guardrails blocked defenders [3]. Concurrently, the platform removed specific community-uploaded models marketed for offensive cyber purposes [5].

## Talking points
* **Ecosystem Independence and Nvidia Partnership:** Discuss how the integration with Nvidia is progressing under DOJ scrutiny, and ensure alignment on maintaining developer trust and open-access distribution channels.
* **Open Source Resilience & Security:** Address the recent cyberattack trends (including risks to third-party API keys highlighted by OpenCode) and discuss Hugging Face's strategy for balancing platform openness with robust safety guardrails [1].
* **Enterprise Adoption:** Explore CEO Clément Delangue's vision that every company will become an AI builder, and evaluate enterprise hesitance regarding closed-source alternatives versus open-source alternatives [3].

## Open questions
* How are regulatory inquiries from the U.S. Department of Justice affecting the timeline and operational independence of the Nvidia-Hugging Face integration?
* What concrete measures or security frameworks is Hugging Face implementing to protect developers from third-party API key compromises and malicious tool-use incidents?
* How does leadership plan to address policy concerns raised by Chief Policy Officer Irene Solaiman regarding pressures to scale back open access due to security risks?

## Sources
* [1] [Hugging Face Warns: 2 Attacks Could Close Open AI](https://shattered.io/hugging-face-solaiman-open-source-ai-cyberattacks-two-attacks-2026)
* [2] [Hugging Face CEO vows to keep fighting for open-source AI after Jensen Huang’s exit](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/12/hugging-face-ceo-vows-to-keep-fighting-for-open-source-ai-after-jensen-huangs-exit)
* [3] [At Miami AI Summit, Hugging Face CEO Clem Delangue predicts every company will become an AI builder - Refresh Miami](https://refreshmiami.com/news/at-miami-ai-summit-hugging-face-ceo-clem-delangue-predicts-every-company-will-necome-an-ai-builder)
* [5] [Hugging Face appears to be hosting a load of models that could be used for cyber attacks](https://www.transformernews.ai/p/hugging-face-appears-to-be-hosting)
